subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these substances has the lowest boiling point?
questions.explain: Simple molecular substances like oxygen have only weak intermolecular forces, so very low boiling points.

questions.q: In which state are particles most closely packed and only able to vibrate in fixed positions?
questions.explain: In a solid, particles are tightly packed in a regular arrangement and only vibrate.

questions.q: What charge does an oxide ion have?
questions.explain: Oxygen gains two electrons to form an O2- ion.

questions.q: Why are metals malleable?
options: Layers of atoms (ions) can slide over each other
questions.explain: Layers of metal ions slide over one another while the metallic bonding holds them together.

questions.q: How many covalent bonds are there in a molecule of methane, CH4?
questions.explain: Carbon forms four single covalent bonds, one to each hydrogen.

questions.q: What charge does a sodium ion have after ionic bonding?
questions.explain: Sodium loses one electron to form a 1+ ion.

questions.q: Why can graphite conduct electricity?
options: Each carbon bonds to four others
It has delocalised electrons between layers
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon bonds to three others, leaving delocalised electrons that carry charge.

questions.q: Graphene is best described as:
options: A simple molecule of two carbons
A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons
questions.explain: Graphene is a single layer of graphite, one atom thick, in a hexagonal arrangement.

questions.q: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
options: They are made of free electrons
Strong electrostatic forces throughout a giant lattice
questions.explain: Strong electrostatic attractions in the giant ionic lattice need lots of energy to break.

questions.q: What allows metals to conduct electricity?
questions.explain: Delocalised electrons in metals are free to move and carry charge.

questions.q: What happens to particles when a substance boils?
options: They gain energy and spread far apart as a gas
questions.explain: Boiling gives particles enough energy to overcome forces and move freely apart as a gas.

questions.q: When do ionic compounds conduct electricity?
options: When molten or dissolved in water
questions.explain: Ions are only free to move and carry charge when the compound is molten or in solution.

questions.q: Silicon dioxide is an example of a:
questions.explain: Silicon dioxide has a giant covalent (macromolecular) structure.

questions.q: In the particle model, what is true of particles in a gas?
options: Far apart and moving quickly in all directions
Touching but able to move past each other
questions.explain: Gas particles are far apart and move randomly at high speed.

questions.q: What happens to particles when a liquid freezes into a solid?
options: They gain energy and move apart
They lose energy and become fixed in a regular arrangement
questions.explain: On freezing, particles lose energy and settle into fixed positions in a regular pattern.

questions.q: Why do metals have high melting points?
options: Strong attraction between metal ions and delocalised electrons
questions.explain: Strong metallic bonding (ions attracted to delocalised electrons) needs much energy to break.

questions.q: Polymers are made of:
options: Many small molecules (monomers) joined into long chains
questions.explain: Polymers are long chains formed by joining many small monomer molecules.

questions.q: Why is graphite soft and slippery?
options: Layers are held together by weak forces and can slide
questions.explain: Weak forces between graphite's layers let them slide over one another.

questions.q: In diamond, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to how many other carbons?
questions.explain: Each carbon in diamond forms four strong covalent bonds, giving a rigid giant structure.

questions.q: Why is diamond unable to conduct electricity?
options: It has no charged particles free to move
Its layers slide over each other
questions.explain: In diamond every electron is held in a covalent bond, so none are free to carry charge.

questions.q: A covalent bond is formed when atoms:
questions.explain: Covalent bonds form when non-metal atoms share pairs of electrons.

questions.q: In ionic bonding, electrons are:
questions.explain: Electrons are transferred from the metal atom to the non-metal atom, forming ions.
